parsed.explanation: The division itself is documented as among the most protective: gender-identity public-accommodations coverage (hotels, restaurants, shops) since 2007, hate-crime penalties, repeal of the panic defence, shield laws enforceable against out-of-state action, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, and no state facility ban. But rule 12 requires starting from the parent regime, which applies here: entry screening instructs officers to refuse or seek extra evidence where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud findings (several governments now issue travel advisories); a federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; official hostility, custody conversion-therapy policy and immigration-custody abuse are national. State statutes are strong, though the dossier supplies no enforcement data for them. Layered state protection raises the division well above the parent, but the universal federal exposures keep it out of Reduced Risk.
